source.title: NASA Open Science Data Repository, Environmental Data Application (EDA), mission RR-9, radiation data: daily absorbed dose on the International Space Station, analysed by the Space Radiation Analysis Group (SRAG) of NASA-JSC.
source.credit: Data and visualizations are courtesy of the Environmental Data Application (EDA) (https://visualization.osdr.nasa.gov/eda/)

note: Fields "gcr", "saa", and "total" of the radiation data of RR-9: the absorbed dose of each day in mGy, from galactic cosmic rays (GCR), from the passes through the South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA), and their sum. The EDA says: "Doses are in water based on standard conversion from dose in silicon" and "preliminary analysis of results from instruments on the International Space Station". We keep the days from the transfer of the animals to the station (2017-08-18) to the undock (2017-09-16): 30 days. Mean: 0.320 mGy for each day (GCR 0.138, SAA 0.181). On 2017-09-11 the GCR part is 0.390 mGy, 3.1 times its median (0.126 mGy). This is the time of the solar particle event that started on 10 September 2017. Instruments on the station measured it: Berger et al., Space Weather 16, 1173–1189 (2018), https://doi.org/10.1029/2018SW001920. The EDA does not label the event, so the link between this value and the event is our reading. The EDA counts the extra dose in the GCR part.
